title: Using a Dictionary
short: Middle Egyptian dictionaries list words in transliteration order, ꜣ j y ꜥ w b p f m n r h ḥ ḫ ẖ z s š q k g t ṯ d ḏ.
trouble: Students look up words with their endings, like nfrt or sḏm.n=f. Look up the root or the base word.

blocks.html: Once you can read a word's consonants, you can look it up. Middle Egyptian dictionaries are ordered by transliteration, in the alphabet you learned in Transliteration and Its Order.

Dictionaries list words in the order ꜣ j y ꜥ w b p f m n r h ḥ ḫ ẖ z s š q k g t ṯ d ḏ, letter by letter. Look up the base word: a verb under its full root (jr.n=f under jrj), a noun under its singular masculine form (nṯrw under nṯr), an adjective under its masculine (nfrt under nfr).

A dictionary cannot list every form of every word; it lists each word once, under a headword. For verbs that means the root, with weak consonants put back, since those are what change from form to form. Endings like .n, .tw, -t, -w and suffix pronouns belong to the grammar, not the dictionary. So before you look a word up, strip it down: take off suffixes and endings, restore any weak j, and you have the headword.

blocks.name: eg-glyphs
blocks.cap: To look up sḏm.n=f, strip the .n and =f: the headword is sḏm.

blocks.title: Which comes first?
blocks.q: Put nfr, ꜣḫ and qd in dictionary order.
steps: Compare first letters: ꜣ is first in the alphabet, n in the middle, q near the end.
So ꜣḫ, then nfr, then qd.

blocks.title: Same first letter
blocks.q: Which comes first, ḥm or ḥtp?
steps: Both begin with ḥ; compare the second letters.
m comes before t in the alphabet.

blocks.html: The standard tools are Raymond O. Faulkner's A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian (1962), small and arranged exactly this way; the great Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache of Adolf Erman and Hermann Grapow (1926–1931), in German, covering all periods; and today the online Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae. In older books z and s are merged, and yod may be written ꞽ or i; check the book's alphabet on its first pages.

Looking up words with their endings. Students search for nfrt or sḏm.n=f and find nothing, or find the wrong entry. Check: before you open the dictionary, strip suffixes and endings and restore weak consonants. Then search for the root.
